name: CA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by six points on the partisan baseline
Ami Bera is a well-funded incumbent with $1.8 million on hand versus Tucker's $16,000
Prediction markets price Bera's win chances around 95 percent
No public general-election polling is available for this race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Bera: a six-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge, with markets pricing his win odds near 95 percent. With no polls to contradict that picture, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would warrant a downgrade toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ami Bera, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Sacramento-area district that leans Democratic by about six points. He has raised $1.25 million and holds $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Robb Tucker has raised roughly $258,000 and reports only $16,000 in cash. No outside groups are actively opposing either candidate, and no public general-election polls are available.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Bera's win probability around 95 percent. With the incumbent advantage, the financial imbalance, and the district's lean all pointing the same direction, the race is rated Safe Democratic, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
